claim: Promptfoo's GitHub Action runs a before-vs-after eval comparison on every PR that modifies a prompt, posting results as a PR comment with an interactive web viewer and caching LLM requests to cut cost.
quote: on every pull request that modifies a prompt ... before vs. after evaluation of edited prompts ... We use caching to speed up subsequent runs. The cache stores LLM requests and outputs, which can be reused in future runs to save cost.

claim: Promptfoo provides CLI/CI-CD integration with declarative configs, deterministic and model-graded assertions, and quality gates that fail the build when prompt quality drops below minimum thresholds; OpenAI acquired Promptfoo in March 2026.
quote: quality gates to enforce minimum performance thresholds ... wire a GitHub Actions gate that fails the build when prompt quality drops

claim: DeepEval plugs into pytest via assert_test() (which raises an assertion error when a metric falls below threshold) and the `deepeval test run` command, which adds 8+ flags over pytest for async, error handling, repeats and identifiers, runnable as a shell step in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI or Jenkins.
quote: assert_test() ... raises an assertion error when a metric falls below its threshold ... deepeval test run adds a range of functionalities on top of Pytest for unit-testing LLMs, enabled by [8+ optional flags]

claim: DeepEval is positioned as a pytest for LLM apps: every push or PR runs the same single-turn or multi-turn, end-to-end or component-level evals locally and in CI, with test suites failing if any metric drops below its threshold to block deployment.
quote: DeepEval plugs into pytest via assert_test() and the deepeval test run command, so every push (or every PR) runs the same evals you'd run locally

claim: In eval-driven development, evals are the working spec: developers maintain golden-set datasets as the regression baseline, change a prompt/model and rerun the eval suite (catching e.g. a tone score dropping 0.85 to 0.72), and CI blocks the change automatically if any metric falls below its gate threshold.
quote: If any metric falls below its threshold at any gate, the CI pipeline blocks the change automatically ... tone score dropped from 0.85 to 0.72 ... production traces that reveal new edge cases get added to golden sets

claim: Braintrust runs eval suites on every PR via a native GitHub Action and blocks changes when metrics fall below thresholds, whereas LangSmith integrates with pytest, Vitest and GitHub workflows but reports results to inform engineers rather than automatically blocking bad releases.
quote: Braintrust integrates with CI/CD through a native GitHub Action that runs eval suites on every pull request. When metrics fall below thresholds, the change is blocked ... LangSmith, where evaluation results inform engineers but do not automatically block bad releases

claim: A practitioner eval pipeline separates offline CI evals (LLM judge plus human review) from online production evals running lightweight deterministic checks under 50ms with 5% async sampling for deeper judging, handles judge flakiness by running twice with swapped positions to detect bias, and gates CI on minPassRate 0.95 / maxRegressions 0.
quote: Run lightweight evals on every response (< 50ms overhead) ... Async: sample 5% for deeper LLM-as-Judge evaluation ... Run twice with swapped positions to eliminate position bias ... minPassRate: 0.95 / maxRegressions: 0

claim: To tame flaky judges, teams define pass bands rather than single thresholds, avoid gating when the judge confidence is below the 0.41-0.60 moderate band, recalibrate the judge monthly or when divergence climbs past ~20-25%, and report pass@k since a 70%-per-trial agent reads ~97% on pass@3 but ~34% on pass^3.
quote: Below the 0.41-0.60 'moderate' band, do not gate on the judge ... a 70%-per-trial agent reads as ~97% on pass@3 but ~34% on pass^3 ... trigger out-of-cycle when you ... see divergence climb past ~20-25%

claim: When LLM-as-judge scorers are flaky or nondeterministic, the guidance is to design for variance rather than pretend determinism: control judge temperature, rerun borderline cases, and reserve repeated judging or ensembles for high-impact decisions.
quote: When judges are flaky or nondeterministic, the goal is not to pretend they are deterministic, but to design for variance: keep the judge temperature controlled when possible, rerun borderline cases, and reserve repeated judging or ensembles for high-impact decisions
